A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LieFlow and retain matching core algorithms, equations and analyses. The complete main texts, appendices, figures and tables support reliable comparison despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic symmetry-discovery experiments, Wasserstein-1 comparisons with LieGAN, and appendix experiments on multiple objects and nonuniform rotations.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and ModelNet10 experiments, including partial symmetries, masked observations, timing comparisons and a time-schedule ablation.

M1.justification: The flow-matching loss, exponential interpolation and transformation-composition procedure remain. V2 adds matrix-composition prior sampling and a Transformer predictor for ModelNet10, and changes the reported synthetic predictors from three-layer GELU MLPs to five-layer ReLU MLPs. Section 4.3 interprets partial symmetries using the existing procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds rotated ModelNet10, partially observed C4, masked point clouds and tilted-axis SO(2) cases. It removes the complex-domain D4 reflection task, the dataset of four synthetic shapes, and the Gaussian-distributed SO(2) rotation case from v1 Appendices C.4–C.5. Icosahedral symmetry was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: LieGAN remains the only baseline family, but its evaluated variants are narrowed within retained comparisons. Table 1 drops the two-generator variant; Table 2 drops the one- and six-generator variants and retains the earlier three-generator results. No new baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: Reported synthetic architecture settings change, and the GL(2) coefficient range changes from uniform [-π/2, π/2] in v1 Appendix B to [-π, π] in v2 Appendix C, with determinant rejection added. New protocols include selecting 100 ModelNet10 objects with 128 points each, masking points, sweeping skewness and comparing training time. These descriptions do not establish that all retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a skewness ablation with training curves, a comparison of GL(2) prior constructions, and tests of missing C4 orientations and masked ModelNet10 observations. The nonuniform SO(2) case study is removed. The existing SO(2)-to-C4 posterior and velocity analysis is retained in Appendix D, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained posterior-entropy plots describe flow behavior rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: New results include 0.428 for the matrix-composition GL(2)-to-C4 prior, 0.118 for synthetic Ico with power scheduling, and ModelNet10 masking errors of 0.156, 0.186 and 0.212. V1's Ico failure is replaced by reported recovery under revised settings. Several inherited scores remain identical, including Tet/Oct/z-axis SO(2) values 0.0885/0.0962/0.0429. Reflection and removed appendix-study results disappear.

T1.justification: New Section 4.3 defines input-dependent symmetry subsets Hx satisfying q(hx)=q(x), and formalizes conditional transformation distributions and their marginalization. The target-field derivation in Appendix A and the posterior-computation derivation and algorithm are retained. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 drops the explicit complex-domain reflection contribution and expands the claimed scope to approximate and partially observed symmetries. ModelNet10 evidence and superiority over LieGAN for discrete groups become central contributions. The distribution-learning formulation and last-minute-convergence contribution remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation based on cancellation of inconsistent targets from nonsymmetry transformations and an interpretation of partial symmetries through conditional distributions. It replaces the Ico failure narrative with recovery using power scheduling, discusses masking robustness and prior sensitivity, and reframes limitations around small point clouds, limited object counts and scalability.

D1.justification: V2 Appendices B–C substantially expand v1's sparse training documentation with dataset construction, network widths, time embeddings, Transformer configuration, optimizers, learning rates and weight decay. They also specify prior construction and rejection rules, an RTX 4090, batch size 512, and per-epoch times of approximately 18 seconds for LieFlow versus 50 for LieGAN.

R1.justification: V2 adds Wu et al. (2015) for ModelNet10 and removes the GELU reference and the Huang and Mangoubi diffusion references. Related work now positions LieGAN alongside Allingham et al. as closest and explains that LieGAN can discover discrete groups with suitably chosen priors. Most cited research is retained.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion, swaps related work and preliminaries, and reorganizes the experiments. The lengthy convergence analysis moves to Appendix D, while dataset, training, scheduling and additional-result material receive separate appendices. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, and Figure 1 is redrawn. V2 regroups 2D histograms, expands 3D visualization panels, splits Table 2 into synthetic and ModelNet10 subtables, and adds masking and skewness tables and curves. Existing diagnostic plots move to Appendix D; reflection and removed case-study displays disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's evaluation and reproducibility through tests on 100 rotated ModelNet10 objects, controlled masking experiments, a quantitative skewness ablation and substantially fuller training details. These provide stronger support beyond hand-built synthetic objects and better justification for the schedule choice. Removing reflection and nonuniform-rotation studies and narrowing LieGAN variants loses useful evidence, but the gains are substantial overall. Repeated-run uncertainty remains unreported.
